q: The Gordon Growth Model values a stock as:
e: Gordon: V = D₁ / (r − g), where D₁ = next dividend, r = required return, g = perpetual growth rate. Constraint: g must be < r.
WACC = blend of cost of equity (from CAPM) and after-tax cost of debt, weighted by market value of equity and debt. Used as the discount rate in DCF.

q: In the WACC formula, the cost of debt is multiplied by (1 − T) because:
e: Interest is tax-deductible, so the after-tax cost of debt is r_d × (1 − T). This 'tax shield' makes debt cheaper than equity (no tax shield on dividends).

e: EV/EBITDA neutralises differences in capital structure (debt vs equity) and depreciation policy. Best for capex-heavy, leveraged industries. P/B is preferred for banks; P/Sales for early-stage; P/NAV for real estate.

q: P/B (Price-to-Book) is most commonly used to value:
e: P/B is the standard valuation multiple for banks because their assets and liabilities are mostly financial (loans, deposits) and book value approximates economic value. Less meaningful for asset-light or intangible-heavy companies.

q: If terminal value accounts for >70% of total enterprise value in a DCF, this is:
o: Always normal — terminal value should dominate
A warning sign — assumptions are very sensitive
e: When terminal value dominates, the valuation is highly sensitive to terminal-growth assumption. Be conservative on g (≤ long-term GDP growth, 3-5%) and cross-check with multiples-based exit value.

q: Which is the appropriate constraint for the Gordon Growth Model?
e: Gordon Model assumes infinite growth at rate g; if g ≥ r, the formula breaks (denominator goes to zero or negative — implies infinite valuation). Always require g < r.

q: The PEG ratio is calculated as:
e: PEG = P/E / Earnings Growth %. PEG of 1 = fairly valued; < 1 may indicate undervaluation given growth; > 1 may suggest premium pricing.

q: Margin of safety in valuation refers to:
o: The minimum return required by SEBI
Buying at a price below your estimated intrinsic value
The buffer in a margin account
e: Margin of safety = buy at a meaningful discount (often 30-50%) to your intrinsic value estimate. Accounts for forecast errors and unforeseen risks. Coined by Benjamin Graham.

q: In a DCF, which of these is the typical proxy for the risk-free rate in India?
e: The 10-year G-Sec yield is the standard proxy for risk-free rate in Indian DCF models. Long maturity matches the long-duration nature of equity cash flows.

q: Equity Value is derived from Enterprise Value by:
o: Subtracting net debt and adding cash
e: Equity Value = Enterprise Value − Net Debt (where Net Debt = Total Debt − Cash & Cash Equivalents). Per-share value = Equity Value / Diluted Shares.

q: The Residual Income Model values equity as:
o: Book value plus PV of future residual income
Sum of dividends discounted to today
e: Residual Income Model: V = Book Value₀ + Σ (RI_t / (1+r)^t), where RI_t = Net Income − r × Book Value. Useful when DCF is messy and dividends are erratic.
